def simulate_snake(board_size, snake, food, moves):
    width, height = board_size
    snake = list(snake)
    food = list(food)
    
    # Direction vectors
    dirs = {
        "UP": (0, -1),
        "DOWN": (0, 1),
        "LEFT": (-1, 0),
        "RIGHT": (1, 0)
    }
    
    # Determine initial current direction based on head and second body part
    if len(snake) > 1:
        current_dir = (snake[0][0] - snake[1][0], snake[0][1] - snake[1][1])
    else:
        current_dir = (1, 0) # Default if snake has length 1
        
    # Map vector back to string direction for opposition check
    vec_to_dir = {v: k for k, v in dirs.items()}
    
    food_eaten = 0
    alive = True
    
    for move in moves:
        if not alive:
            break
            
        requested_dir = dirs[move]
        
        # Check if the requested direction is opposite to the current direction
        # Opposite means (dx1 + dx2 == 0 and dy1 + dy2 == 0)
        if (requested_dir[0] + current_dir[0] == 0) and (requested_dir[1] + current_dir[1] == 0):
            # Move in current direction instead
            move_dir = current_dir
        else:
            move_dir = requested_dir
            current_dir = requested_dir
            
        # Calculate new head position
        new_head = (snake[0][0] + move_dir[0], snake[0][1] + move_dir[1])
        
        # Check boundaries
        if not (0 <= new_head[0] < width and 0 <= new_head[1] < height):
            alive = False
            break
            
        # Check self-collision
        # The snake can't hit its own tail if the tail is going to move away, 
        # unless it didn't eat food and the tail doesn't move? Wait: 
        # "touches any part of the snake's own body (other than the tail square it is about to move)"
        # If the snake doesn't eat food, the tail moves (gets removed). So the tail square is safe.
        # If the snake eats food, the tail stays (doesn't move), meaning the tail IS part of the body.
        # Thus, the body to check against for collision is all parts except the tail (if tail moves) 
        # or all parts (if tail stays).
        
        # Check food collision before modifying snake
        ate_food = False
        if food and new_head == food[0]:
            ate_food = True
            
        # Determine body check set
        # If we eat food, tail stays, so we check against ALL current snake segments.
        # If we don't eat food, tail moves, so we check against all segments EXCEPT the last one.
        body_to_check = snake if ate_food else snake[:-1]
        
        if new_head in body_to_check:
            alive = False
            break
            
        # Move snake
        snake.insert(0, new_head)
        
        if ate_food:
            food.pop(0)
            food_eaten += 1
        else:
            snake.pop()
            
    return (snake, alive, food_eaten)
